articles.headline: The Fall of the Fellowship
articles.deck: A lament in three stanzas for Frodo, Sam and a Shire that never saw Satoru coming.
articles.caption: *Satoru Umezawa* — and a nightmare or two.
body: Some games deserve a match report. This one deserved a lament. The night’s second game ran twelve rounds and two hours and five minutes — among the longest the pod has played this year. Sem went first with *Frodo, Adventurous Hobbit* and *Sam, Loyal Attendant*; Bart brought *Teval, the Balanced Scale*, Raoul *Monk Gyatso*, and Mauro *Satoru Umezawa*. Our poet laureate filed the rest in verse.

verse: Twelve rounds of battle, two hours of pain,
The Hobbits marched boldly, but all was in vain.
Frodo clutched his ring, Sam readied the stew,
But Satoru emerged with a nightmare or two.
No second breakfast, no glorious feast,
Just Hobbits reduced to bugs for the beast.
With curses and creatures, he crushed every plan,
Not even the Ring could save Frodo and Sam.
Bart watched the chaos, Raoul held his ground,
While Satoru’s terror spread all around.
The Shire fell silent, the Fellowship slain⁠—
Next time, bring removal. Or don’t queue again. 💀🍃

body.flavor: A ring makes you invisible. It does not make you safe.

body: Satoru now stands at four wins from eleven games for Mauro. The table named *Hullbreaker Horror* card of the match.

articles.headline: Living Death Crowns Celes, Then Sokka Storms the Night
articles.deck: Patrick ends the opener with one massive reanimation; Sem turns six gifted cards into one long, decisive turn.
articles.caption: *Sokka, Tenacious Tactician* leads the charge.
body: The shuffling had barely stopped on Thursday night when the first warnings went out. Lennart, sleeving up *Koma, World-Eater* for the very first time, took the opening turn. Sem brought *Rendmaw, Creaking Nest*, Toon the fearsome *Indoraptor, the Perfect Hybrid*. But the name everybody kept glancing at was Patrick’s *Celes, Rune Knight*.

They were right to. Celes was a threat from the opening turns, and nobody at the table could say they hadn’t been warned. Yet the real story of the game was *Slagstorm*. It stopped every player at the table — every player except Celes. While the others were knocked back again and again, Patrick’s knight stood untouched, and the graveyards around the table kept filling up.

Then came the finale. After nearly an hour and a half, Patrick cast a massive *Living Death*. Every creature on the battlefield went to the graveyard, and every creature card in the graveyards came roaring back at once — with the biggest army of all on Patrick’s side of the table. There was no answer left. Eight rounds, one knight, one very full board.

body.flavor: The fallen do not rest. Not while I still stand.

body: It was Celes’s first win in six outings — proof that patience is a deck strategy too. The table voted *Slagstorm* card of the match, and nobody argued: it held the whole pod in check, with one notable exception.

The second game was quicker, but no less dramatic. Toon went first with *Sokrates, Athenian Teacher*, Lennart switched to *Ghyrson Starn, Kelermorph*, and Patrick reached for *Cloud, Ex-SOLDIER*. Sem sat down behind *Sokka, Tenacious Tactician*.

Then came a lesson nobody had asked for. Sokrates handed Sem six cards — a gift, in the philosopher’s eyes. Sem saw ammunition. What followed was one long turn, the kind where the rest of the table starts doing the maths on whether they will ever see another one. Long, yes. But game-winning.

body.flavor: A good plan uses what you’re given. A great plan uses what they give you.

body: Seven rounds and just under an hour after it began, it was over, and *Sokrates* — fittingly — was named card of the match. Sokka now stands at two wins from three games for Sem.

articles.headline: Xyris Shakes the Pod, But Falls to Yshtola
articles.deck: Impact Tremors send two opponents packing, though the Grand Archenemy proves too much in the end.
articles.caption: Xyris, the Tide’s Voice, unleashed her power — and the ground shook.
body: Four commanders took their seats for the opener: Raoul’s *Xyris*, Patrick’s *Y’shtola, Night’s Blessed*, Lennart’s *Skullbriar, the Walking Grave* and Sem’s *Don Andres, the Renegade*. Patrick had the first turn.

Last night’s first Commander game started with *Xyris, the Tide’s Voice* at the helm, and it didn’t take long before the table felt the pressure. With a well-timed *Impact Tremors*, Xyris turned every spell into a threat, sending two opponents packing in spectacular fashion.

The first casualty fell to a massive wave of damage, as the tremors rippled through the battlefield. Not long after, the second player was swept away as well, unable to recover from the repeated shocks. What looked like a sure path to victory for Xyris quickly became a two-player showdown.
But when it came down to the final duel, Xyris ran out of steam. Facing *Yshtola, the Grand Archenemy*, the tide turned.

Yshtola’s relentless card advantage, combined with her signature control and value, outpaced Xyris in the late game. Despite a valiant effort and a board full of sea creatures, Xyris couldn’t close the deal, and the Grand Archenemy claimed the win.

body.quote: “Impact Tremors did exactly what I hoped — it just wasn’t enough in the end,” said Xyris’s pilot after the game. “Yshtola was on another level.”

body: A stunning start, a hard-fought finish, and a reminder that in Commander, even the most explosive openings can’t always outlast a true archenemy.

body.flavor: The storm does not care who started it. It only cares who is left standing.

articles.headline: Marchesa Shows No Mercy in Bracket 4 Brawl
articles.deck: All players face the Black Rose, who comes back stronger after a devastating board wipe.
articles.caption: Marchesa, the Black Rose — elegant, ruthless, and always one step ahead.
body: Lennart sleeved up *Marchesa, the Black Rose* for the nightcap, facing Raoul’s *Zimone, Mystery Unraveler*, Patrick’s *Cloud, Ex-SOLDIER* and Sem’s *Sokka, Tenacious Tactician*. Raoul went first; it would take ten rounds and more than an hour and a half to settle.

The second game of the night was a true test of resilience, as all players lined up against a bracket 4 *Marchesa, the Black Rose*. From the very first turn, it was clear: this wouldn’t be an easy victory. Marchesa’s aristocratic charm quickly turned into lethal control, draining life, duplicating creatures, and building an overwhelming board presence.
Midway through the game, things looked grim for Marchesa when the table finally managed to coordinate a board wipe. For a moment, it seemed like her threat had been neutralized.

body.flavor: Every rose returns in spring. Mine return by evening.

body: But as so often happens with *Marchesa, the Black Rose*, that was just a setback. She returned from the graveyard stronger than before, bringing back key pieces, reassembling her engine, and immediately regaining momentum.

What followed was a masterclass in inevitability. With every creature, every drain, and every political nudge, Marchesa wrapped the game back under her control. In the end, no one could stop the Black Rose, and she claimed the win — once again.

body.quote: “She died, she came back, and she just had more resources than anyone else,” said one of the defeated players. “Bracket 4 is no joke.”
